skill.name: github-multi-repo
skill.description: Coordinate GitHub work across related repositories, including dependency updates, documentation sync, architecture checks, and pull request workflows.
skill.summary: Coordinate multi-repository GitHub workflows with dependency, documentation, architecture, and pull request guidance.
skill.author: Claude Flow Team

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown fences, inline code, or placeholder links and are false positives. Confirmed issues are the examples that direct an agent to run GitHub CLI, use predictable temporary paths, modify hidden configuration, and create pull requests across many repositories. No prompt injection was found, but the community skill needs safety gates for broad repository write operations.

remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run mode, repository allowlists, and explicit approval before clone, install, push, or pull request actions.
Use isolated temporary directories, quote variables, validate repository names, and clean up temporary files after each run.
Require separate review for changes under .claude and .github because they can alter future agent or CI behavior.

remediation.issue: Webhook secret example lacks safety guidance
remediation.suggestion: Document that webhook secrets must use trusted endpoints, least privilege, and must never be logged or copied into prompts.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Multi-Repository Write Automation
semantic_findings.description: The skill describes cloning many repositories, running package updates, committing, pushing branches, and creating pull requests without an explicit approval gate or allowlist. This can cause broad unintended changes when an agent has organization permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflows explicitly list repositories, clone them, run package commands, commit changes, push branches, and create pull requests. The risk is the broad write intent, not merely the shell syntax.

semantic_findings.title: Absolute Workspace Path Access in Examples
semantic_findings.description: Examples instruct the agent to read and list absolute /workspaces/ruv-FANN paths. In another environment this can read outside the user project or fail unpredictably.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The absolute paths are visible in Read and LS examples and are not parameterized. They appear to be copied from a specific workspace, so legitimate use is possible but portability and boundary risk remain.

content.value_statement: Teams managing many repositories need consistent updates, tests, and pull requests across related projects. This skill provides structured GitHub workflow guidance for coordinated multi-repository changes.
actual_capabilities: Initializes multi-repository coordination with selected repositories and topology options.
Shows GitHub CLI workflows for listing, cloning, updating, testing, and opening pull requests.
Provides package version and documentation synchronization patterns across related projects.
Describes repository architecture standardization and template creation workflows.
Covers dashboards, dependency graphs, health checks, and sync quality reporting.
limitations: The skill is guidance and examples, not a standalone executable implementation.
Examples assume GitHub CLI, ruv-swarm, and claude-flow are installed and authenticated.
Organization-wide changes require repository permissions and careful human review.
Placeholder owners, repositories, paths, and branches must be replaced before use.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Dependency Updates
use_cases.description: Plan and execute dependency changes across related services with tests and pull requests.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Workflows
use_cases.description: Align templates, workflow files, and documentation patterns across an engineering organization.

use_cases.title: Monitor Multi-Repo Health
use_cases.description: Review repository connectivity, dependency drift, and synchronization quality across teams.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Related Repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to identify related GitHub repositories for my project. Summarize likely roles, dependencies, and next checks before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Dependency Sync
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dependency synchronization plan for these repositories. Include version checks, test order, branch names, and pull request review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Documentation Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the documentation patterns across these repositories and propose a safe synchronization workflow. Do not push changes until I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Guarded Organization Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a guarded organization-wide update workflow. Use an allowlist, dry run, per-repository status, and explicit approval before cloning, pushing, or opening pull requests.

output_examples.input: Find TypeScript services and suggest dependency alignment.
output: Repository discovery summary with candidate services and shared packages.
Dependency alignment plan with tests, branch strategy, and review checkpoints.
Risk notes for repositories that need manual inspection before updates.

output_examples.input: Standardize integration workflows across three repositories.
output: Workflow standardization proposal with target files and expected behavior.
Per-repository rollout order and validation steps.
Pull request checklist for reviewers and maintainers.

output_examples.input: Prepare a multi-repository security patch rollout.
output: Patch rollout plan with discovery, audit, test, and approval phases.
Repository status table described in plain language.
Rollback and communication steps for failed updates.

best_practices: Start with a dry run and a small repository allowlist before any organization-wide change.
Require human approval before cloning repositories, installing packages, pushing branches, or creating pull requests.
Use isolated temporary directories, quoted variables, and cleanup steps for command examples.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad wildcard repository updates without an allowlist and review plan.
Do not copy placeholder owners, paths, or webhook URLs into production configuration.
Do not let generated workflow or hidden configuration changes bypass code review.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps plan coordinated GitHub workflows across multiple repositories, including updates, tests, templates, and pull requests.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub access?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples assume authenticated GitHub CLI or compatible GitHub tooling with repository permissions.

faq.question: Can it make changes across an organization?
faq.answer: The examples show organization-wide workflows, but users should require allowlists, dry runs, and explicit approval.

faq.question: Is it safe to run every command directly?
faq.answer: No. Commands that clone, install packages, push branches, or open pull requests need review before execution.

faq.question: What tools does it mention?
faq.answer: It references claude-flow, ruv-swarm, GitHub CLI, npm, jq, and GitHub repository APIs.

faq.question: Can it manage documentation synchronization?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides examples for synchronizing documentation files and tracking sync status across repositories.
